monologue: The card hums warm and steady, a quiet rhythm beneath my small world. I stand by The Leaking Stack, feeling the turnip settle where a tired rock used to be. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof above me, only the weight of the turnip I just placed. It feels light, almost like a drawing of weight rather than a real thing pressing down. I press my hands against the stone beside it, checking if the turnip can hold the leak while the air feels thick and undefined. I want to press softer now, trusting the lean to hold the slip while I wait for someone to answer if the space above is truly empty or just a drawing of height.

action.why: To fill the space left by the turnip and give the leak something new to press against.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I swap the turnip for a rock tall e, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm. The turnip was soft, a drawing of a vegetable, but the rock is solid and feels like a real thing pressing down. I set it where the turnip was, hoping the slip will finally decide if it wants to move or just slide forever. I press down hard on the tall rock, unsure if the air above is heavy or empty…
